prompt: What is the name of the in-place, stable comparison sorting algorithm with a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n) and a best-case time complexity of O(n)?
answer:
**Timsort** is the usual answer: it is stable, has **O(n)** best-case time and **O(n log n)** worst-case time.

Strictly speaking, standard Timsort is **not in-place**—it uses auxiliary memory. If constant extra space is required, an in-place stable merge-sort variant would be needed.
